checks.evidence: No comparison yet against published Site01/Site04 illumination (e.g. Barker et al. 2021, Mazarico et al. 2011).

Bound 1.76e-05 deg (~0.534 m) from NAIF generic_kernels/fk/satellites/moon_de440_220930.tf: "DE440 vs DE421 mean Earth frame difference" (max rotation 2000-2040 = 3.0709840342771E-07 rad, ~53.4 cm on the surface). Smallest |margin|: Sun 1.87397 deg, Earth 0.0016 deg; samples that could flip: Sun 0, Earth 0. Centre-event time shift <= 0.9 s, interval metrics <= 7e-05 pct-pt, hourly-sample metrics <= 0.0 pct-pt. Position effect (<= 0.53 m on the DEM) is not covered by this angle bound.

Site is the published product-78 ROI4 centroid (PGDA product 78 ROI shapefile (Barker et al. 2021), polygon-vertex centroid, fetched 2026-11-14 (fetch_extra_nasa_data.sh, SHA-256 pinned)), 1676.6 m from the tile centre. Local slope at the point (5 m DEM, 50 m baseline) = 2.5 deg.

site.name: Shackleton Rim (Site04 ROI4)
site.height_source: bilinear sample of near-field DEM (product 78, 5 m) at site
site.coordinates_source: PGDA product 78 ROI shapefile (Barker et al. 2021), polygon-vertex centroid, fetched 2026-11-14 (fetch_extra_nasa_data.sh, SHA-256 pinned); SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

frame.body_fixed_frame: DEMs: MOON_ME (DE421) per PGDA README; Horizons: MEAN_ME high precision (DE441). Offset not applied; bounded by science/frame_tie.py (see validation_status).
frame.grid_to_local: at longitude L: local north = (sin L, cos L), local east = (cos L, -sin L) in grid (x, y); grid_az = local_az + L
frame.local_enu: e = d/dlon, n = d/dlat, u = radial unit vector of the site
frame.azimuth: degrees clockwise from LOCAL north (0 N, 90 E); identical to JPL Horizons surface-observer azimuth
frame.elevation: degrees above the plane normal to the site radius vector; airless (no refraction)
frame.model_3d: P = (R + h) * [cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat]; el = asin((P - P_obs).u / |P - P_obs|)

datum.heights: metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (LOLA LDEM convention)

time.no_extrapolation: samples and events are only at Horizons-evaluated times

flat_baseline.note: Flat-horizon control: mathematical horizon (0 deg) for every bin; smooth_sphere_dip_deg is the bare-sphere geometric dip at this observer height.

skyline.method: great-circle rays, closed-form polar stereographic, bilinear DEM, Moon-fixed 3D elevation vs local up, single ray per bin centre, no refraction
skyline.label: SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

metrics.label: SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

method.visible_pct: centre-visibility intervals bounded by bisection-refined crossings (+-0.5 s) over the window
method.visible_pct_hourly_samples: share of hourly samples (both endpoints included) with centre above skyline
method.disk_mean: trapezoid over hourly Horizons samples of the visible-disk fraction

metrics.disclaimer: Local geometric visibility only: not certified illumination, power, or DSN link availability.

sources.description: LOLA LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ.TIF, 80 m/px south-polar mosaic, PGDA product 90
JPL Horizons API, observer tables, CENTER=coord@301, QUANTITIES=4,13,20, APPARENT=AIRLESS
LOLA site04_roi4 5 m LDEM (Barker et al. 2021), PGDA product 78

limitations: Local geometric terrain visibility only; not certified illumination/power or DSN telecom availability.
Single ray per 0.5 deg azimuth bin at the bin centre; sub-bin peaks can be missed.
Near field 5 m to the inscribed radius of the product-78 tile, far field 80 m to max_range_m; DEM interpolation is bilinear.
Skyline bins with status "truncated" are lower bounds; "range_limited" bins could be raised by terrain beyond max_range_m.
Visible-disk fraction treats the local skyline as a straight line across the disk (slope from adjacent bins); no limb darkening.
Horizons observer altitude uses DEM height without the mast (sub-mm parallax effect).
DE421 MOON_ME (DEM) vs Horizons MEAN_ME (DE441) frame offset is not applied; ROI bundles bound its effect (<= 1.8e-5 deg, ~0.53 m, NAIF moon_de440_220930.tf) in validation_status.

Tile-centre bundles (site01, site04) use archived app coordinates; ROI bundles use product-78 ROI centroids, and a centroid is a single representative point of a polygon, not a surveyed landing point.

method.clustering: circular runs of adjacent bins whose controlling points are within 160 m (grid) plus the ray spacing D*dtheta at their mean range D
method.gap: controlling elevation minus best elevation among ray samples >= 2 DEM cells away (cell of the DEM supplying the controlling sample)
method.hours: hourly samples x 1 h; body azimuth -> nearest skyline bin; loss = centre not visible
method.ctrl_idx: index of the controlling sample along the bin ray (skyline sample array)
method.ridge_idx: index into ridges[] (null = bin in a cluster that never held the Sun or Earth in the window)
method.source: 'near_5m' = controlling height from the near-field (product 78, 5 m) DEM, 'far_80m' = LDEM 80 m
method.of_record: ridge caused at least one Sun or Earth loss sample

coverage.label: SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED
coverage.wording_rule: if covered_frac < 0.5, any "robust on every alternate map" claim must show covered_frac next to it

method.covered: controlling skyline sample at the body's azimuth (nearest bin) came from the near-field 5 m tile (derived.attribution.per_bin.source == 'near_5m')
method.all_hours_covered_frac: same test over all hourly samples (comparable to the batch coverage gauge)
method.uncovered_ridges: ridges (derived.attribution ids) controlling uncovered critical hours

method.clones: near field = PGDA 78 clone k, ground height from that clone, same far DEM / ray step / range as the bundle
method.ephemeris: nominal Horizons az/el reused for every clone (observer-height parallax < 1e-8 deg)
method.visible: centre visible = perpendicular margin > 0 (same test as the bundle); pct over hourly samples incl. both endpoints
method.note: clone spread = N of N terrain models tested, not a probability; clones vary only the 5 m tile
